column1: # Canonical rendering of core values — the contract both engines are held to.
# The differential compares SUCCESS rows by canonical render, so a divergence
# here is a divergence the engine-level gate would report as a hard failure.

column3: int64 max renders exactly, no float rounding
no digit grouping in the canonical form
None is spelled none, and is its own sole inhabitant

column1: # --- type literals (REFERENCE.md: type names push type-literal values) ---
# Rendered as the PARSEABLE `0d…` form with the sign BEFORE the marker, so
# the render round-trips as the same value and a BigInteger is never
# mistaken for an Integer. core/ts had both TYPES and neither constructor
# nor render arm, so every one of these printed as a bare number.

column3: beyond int64 — exact, no float rounding
plain 'f' form at every magnitude — never scientific
below 1e-6, where JS String goes exponential — still plain here
the exact magnitude at which JS String flips to an exponent

column1: # --- the collection barrier and typed containers survive canon ---
# `end` is the word and `;` its synonym (REFERENCE.md:415), so canon of the
# marker is `end` — rendering it empty loses the barrier and the source no
# longer parses back the same. Typed containers keep their type tag
# (REFERENCE.md:228); `deq` is specified to IGNORE that tag (:1224), which
# is only meaningful because the tag is on the value.

column3: the collection barrier is a value with a source form
the tag survives an EMPTY typed list — [] would lose it
an unresolved type name is still a bare Word here (ADR-012 rule 4)
the untagged twin — distinguishable, as deq's carve-out requires
the tag survives an EMPTY typed map
word-tagged twin of the typed-list row
the /q group modifier renders in source form, not as a word payload
and so does /r — the two engines rendered two different debug spellings here
a negative fractional keeps BOTH its sign placement and its scale
a zero significand still carries its scale — not collapsed to 0d0
far below binary64's range — exact, where a float underflows to zero
far above it — exact, where a float overflows to Infinity
a stray close paren has a source form — rendering it empty drops the token
